source.title: What Learning Systems do Intelligent Agents Need? Complementary Learning Systems Theory Updated

confidence_rationale: The modern CLS restatement, co-authored by the DeepMind team that put replay at the centre of agent design. Directly supports two of MECH-423's readiness sub-conditions: replay is the mechanism by which experience statistics are integrated across the system (R3), and neocortical learning can be RAPID when new information is consistent with existing shared structure -- i.e. the super-additive regime is precisely 'schema-consistent' integration. Explicitly bridges neuroscience and ML agent design, which is the exact cross-domain register MECH-423 lives in. Mapping fidelity moderate because it is a review, not a controlled super-additivity test.
failure_signatures: If replayed experience is not weighted/selected to interleave across the modules that share the latent, integration does not accrue and the integrated arm shows no advantage -- replay merely rehearses within-module and the cross-pollination MECH-423 predicts never occurs.

When new information is INCONSISTENT with the existing shared structure, neocortical (slow, shared) integration is slow and can interfere; super-additivity is expected only in the schema-consistent regime, so a mismatched module pairing can produce a null or negative result that is about task-relatedness, not about integration machinery.

mapping.source_claim_statement: CLS updated: replay of hippocampal memories allows goal-dependent weighting of experience statistics and is the route by which structured knowledge is built; neocortical learning can be rapid for information consistent with known structure; the framework is explicitly relevant to designing artificial intelligent agents.
mapping.ree_translation: Supports MECH-423's readiness conditions R3 (replay actively moving/weighting traces across modules) and sharpens the super-additive regime: the integrated arm should beat the additive baseline specifically when the modules share schema-consistent structure over the L-space latent. REE's MECH-121 replay is the 'goal-dependent weighting' engine; the claim is that it must be running for cross-module gain to appear.
mapping.mapping_caveat: A review/position paper, not a controlled experiment measuring a super-additive margin. It establishes that replay is the integration route and that schema-consistency gates the speed of gain, but the magnitude (gain EXCEEDING the sum) is not quantified here. The 'intelligent agent' framing is aspirational, not a benchmark.
mapping.source_context: Cognitive neuroscience + AI; hippocampal replay, systems consolidation, deep RL agent design (DQN-era DeepMind).

confidence_components.notes: High-impact review in a top venue, authoritative authorship spanning exactly the neuro/ML bridge MECH-423 occupies. Held below 0.8 because review-level evidence and the super-additive magnitude is asserted-as-plausible, not measured.
